user_prompt:
method match_parens(lst: seq<string>) returns (result: string)
    requires |lst| == 2 // Ensure that the input list contains exactly two strings
    requires forall i: int :: 0 <= i < |lst| ==> (forall j: int :: 0 <= j < |lst[i]| ==> (lst[i][j] == '(' || lst[i][j] == ')')) // Strings contain only '(' and ')'
    ensures result == "Yes" ==> (exists order: int :: order == 0 || order == 1 ==> is_good_string(lst[order] + lst[1 - order])) // If the result is 'Yes', at least one concatenation results in a good string
    ensures result == "No" ==> (forall order: int :: order == 0 || order == 1 ==> !is_good_string(lst[order] + lst[1 - order])) // If the result is 'No', no concatenation results in a good string

// Helper function to determine if a string is a good string
function is_good_string(s: string): bool
    requires forall i: int :: 0 <= i < |s| ==> (s[i] == '(' || s[i] == ')') // Ensure the string only contains parentheses
    ensures result == true ==> (count_open(s) == count_close(s)) // A good string must have balanced open and close parentheses
    ensures result == false ==> (count_open(s) != count_close(s)) // A string that is not good has unbalanced parentheses

function count_open(s: string): int
    ensures result >= 0 // The count of open parentheses is non-negative
    ensures result == |{ i: int | 0 <= i < |s| && s[i] == '(' }| // Count the number of '(' in the string

function count_close(s: string): int
    ensures result >= 0 // The count of close parentheses is non-negative
    ensures result == |{ i: int | 0 <= i < |s| && s[i] == ')' }| // Count the number of ')' in the string
